_note: Skeleton for docs/board-intake-exemptions.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_board_intake_recorded.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add an entry ONLY when an intake row's subject names an issue that lives on ANOTHER repository and the row declares no `repo` ref for the predicate to read. That is the bar: the row is LAWFUL and is not corrected, because its refs are PUBLISHED and immutable (docs/instruments/ledger.md §9.1) and a `repo` ref added after the fact would record a declaration that was never made — the no-backfill family (§9.12) — so no truthful value restores the scope. This is the same TRUTHFULNESS bar as docs/close-board-exemptions.example.json, and `bar` is a DECLARATION KEY WITH ONE LAWFUL VALUE, `no-truthful-value`, which the loader REQUIRES and refuses every other value for, so a falsified ground cannot be re-stated as data. Key every entry by the row's own `n` — the value the gate reads — so a FUTURE intake row (a different `n`) can never be excused by it; a short or invented key matches nothing while looking like it should. `reason` and `proof` are both REQUIRED: the proof must be the external receipt that the named issue is REAL and OPEN ON THE OTHER REPOSITORY (e.g. `gh issue view <N> --repo <owner/name> --json state,url` reading OPEN) AND that the same number resolves to nothing on this board — an exemption states that the row names a cross-repo item, never that the row is wrong. `domain` must be the declared value 'the intake row names an issue on another repository and declares no repo ref'. It is printed as an 'excused:' line with its reason and proof on EVERY gate run, so it is a visible debt rather than forgiveness. A malformed entry, or one that matches NO violation, is a gate ERROR rather than a silent pass. Absent or empty means NO exemptions and is the shipped state. Expect this list to stay near-empty: the remedy for a SECOND entry is the writer rule, not a second row — every cross-repo intake row from here MUST carry a `repo` ref naming the other repository (docs/instruments/ledger.md §9.5). That rule is UNENFORCED BY CONSTRUCTION and is stated rather than implied: the omission is indistinguishable at the bytes from an ordinary in-repo intake row, so no gate can uphold it, and a future cross-repo row without one re-opens the same defect.
